principle: Look-up table of state-action values (Q-learning, SARSA)
advantages: Simple, interpretable, low compute, converges for small problems
limitations: Curse of dimensionality; needs coarse state discretisation; poor generalisation
best_application: Isolated intersections, embedded controllers with few states

principle: Neural network approximates Q-values (DQN, DDQN, D3QN, dueling, PER)
advantages: Handles rich states (queues, positions, images); discrete phase actions fit naturally; mature tooling
limitations: Overestimation, instability, sample inefficiency; exploration on live streets unsafe
best_application: Phase selection at single or loosely coupled intersections

principle: Directly optimises a stochastic policy (REINFORCE, PPO, TRPO)
advantages: Stable updates (PPO); continuous or duration actions possible

principle: Actor (policy) + critic (value) learned jointly (A2C, A3C, DDPG, SAC, MA2C, MAPPO)
advantages: Lower variance than pure PG; natural for multi-agent CTDE

principle: Learns or uses a traffic model for planning/imagination
advantages: Sample efficiency; can embed traffic-flow knowledge; safer exploration
best_application: Settings where interaction data are scarce

principle: High-level policy sets goals/regions, low-level agents control signals
advantages: Scalability to large networks; temporal abstraction
limitations: Design complexity; credit assignment across levels

principle: Learns to adapt quickly to new intersections/demand (MetaLight, transfer)
limitations: Training cost; task distribution must cover reality
best_application: Rolling out to many heterogeneous intersections

principle: Learns from logged data without online exploration
advantages: No risky online exploration; uses historical detector logs
limitations: Distribution shift; requires good logged data

principle: Large language model reasons about traffic state; policy refined with RL/critic feedback
limitations: Latency and compute; hallucination; limited safety guarantees
